description: Dabiz Muñoz's maximalist Madrid flagship remains the city's defining global fine-dining address. The room at NH Collection Madrid Eurobuilding is theatrical, irreverent and intensely polished, with a long tasting menu that folds Asian references, Spanish produce and surreal presentation into one of Europe's most singular luxury meals.
highlights: Madrid's three-star and World’s 50 Best anchor, known for edible theatre, Asian-Spanish creativity and a high-energy luxury dining room.
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; La Liste; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Quique Dacosta's Madrid restaurant gives the Mandarin Oriental Ritz a refined contemporary-Spanish flagship worthy of the hotel's grand setting. The cooking is elegant, technically exact and tailored to an international luxury clientele, with tasting menus that translate Dacosta's Mediterranean vocabulary into a formal capital-city dining room.
highlights: Two-star hotel fine dining in the restored Ritz, combining grand architecture, polished service and contemporary Spanish haute cuisine.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official hotel website; Mandarin Oriental

description: Dani García's intimate fire-led counter at Hyatt Regency Hesperia Madrid is one of the city's most concentrated luxury dining experiences. A small number of guests sit close to the action while smoke, embers and Japanese-inflected technique shape a disciplined, high-impact tasting menu.
highlights: Boutique two-star room focused on flame, smoke, counter intimacy and a polished hotel setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Set inside Casino de Madrid, Paco Roncero's flagship is a polished expression of Spanish avant-garde cooking in one of the city's most elegant historic buildings. The experience balances tasting-menu theatre, a serious wine program and a terrace setting that appeals strongly to affluent visitors seeking a grand Madrid night out.
highlights: Two-star avant-garde dining inside Casino de Madrid, with a Jaime Hayon-designed room and a celebrated terrace.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Diego Guerrero's DSTAgE remains one of Madrid's most influential contemporary tasting-menu restaurants. The experience is creative without feeling stiff, moving through an industrial-chic space that suits diners looking for serious cooking with a more modern, urban rhythm.
highlights: Two-star creative dining in a converted industrial-style room, with a strong chef identity and contemporary Madrid energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Mario Sandoval's Coque is a large-format destination restaurant that turns dinner into a sequence of spaces, wines and culinary moments. The Madrid address combines a two-star kitchen, a serious family-run hospitality culture and a striking modern interior that feels built for special occasions.
highlights: Two-star destination restaurant with a multi-space experience, major cellar and polished contemporary Spanish cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Ramón Freixa's atelier is one of Madrid's most exclusive new-generation fine-dining rooms, built around a tiny counter-style experience for a handful of guests. Its Barrio de Salamanca location, polished design and highly personal cooking make it especially relevant to diners seeking intimacy, rarity and luxury-level service.
highlights: Two-star 10-seat atelier in Barrio de Salamanca, designed for an intimate and highly controlled gourmet experience.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Saddle is a contemporary Madrid luxury restaurant with the bones of a classic grand address. The service, wine program and room design give it strong appeal for business dinners, elegant celebrations and guests who want Michelin-level cooking without avant-garde excess.
highlights: One-star luxury restaurant in Chamberí, known for polished service, a serious cellar and a balance of classic and contemporary cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Desde 1911 translates the seafood authority of Pescaderías Coruñesas into a serene, high-end Madrid dining room. The restaurant is prized for pristine fish, meticulous service and a sense of old-school luxury updated for contemporary affluent diners.
highlights: One-star seafood destination from Pescaderías Coruñesas, with pristine product, a garden setting and highly polished service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Eater; Official restaurant website

description: RavioXO is Dabiz Muñoz's irreverent, high-energy restaurant dedicated to pasta, dumplings and boundary-crossing Asian-Spanish flavors. It feels less formal than DiverXO but still belongs firmly in the luxury dining conversation thanks to its ambition, price point and international pull.
highlights: One-star creative dumpling and pasta restaurant with the theatrical XO identity and a sleek urban setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: OSA brings a discreet destination-restaurant feeling to the Manzanares riverside, away from the most obvious hotel and shopping districts. The small chalet setting, open kitchen and strong cellar give the restaurant a calm, personal luxury that contrasts with Madrid's larger gastronomic stages.
highlights: One-star riverside chalet with an intimate room, modern cooking and a strong sense of personal hospitality.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: CEBO gives Hotel Urban a sophisticated fine-dining room close to Madrid's museum and luxury-hotel circuit. The cooking is contemporary and product-focused, while the setting offers the kind of polished central address that works well for both visiting gourmets and business travelers.
highlights: One-star hotel restaurant near the Prado and Puerta del Sol, with contemporary Spanish cooking and a refined central setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Ricardo Sanz Wellington remains a benchmark for Japanese-Spanish luxury dining in Madrid. Inside the Hotel Wellington, the restaurant pairs sushi-bar precision with Mediterranean product and the polish expected from one of the capital's classic five-star hotels.
highlights: One-star Japanese-Mediterranean dining inside Hotel Wellington, with sushi-counter finesse and luxury-hotel service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: A'Barra is a polished product-led restaurant where service, wine and technical precision matter as much as the kitchen's seasonal Spanish repertoire. It is a strong fit for affluent diners who want a serious Michelin dinner in a restrained, elegant room rather than a theatrical tasting-menu environment.
highlights: One-star product-led restaurant with an elegant dining room, refined service and a strong nature-driven culinary identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Ugo Chan is one of Madrid's most compelling Japanese-Spanish fine-dining restaurants, marrying sushi discipline with Iberian instinct. The room is intimate and focused, the product is strong and the experience feels especially relevant for diners who want contemporary Madrid beyond classic Spanish formats.
highlights: One-star Japanese-Spanish restaurant in Chamartín, known for precision, product and a personal chef-driven identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Edwin Rodríguez's Quimbaya gives Madrid a polished Colombian fine-dining address with a clear cultural identity. The restaurant is intimate, technically ambitious and distinctive within the city's Michelin landscape, making it a strong choice for international diners seeking something beyond the usual European tasting-menu language.
highlights: One-star Colombian signature cuisine in Chamberí, with a clear narrative, refined service and an intimate urban room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Rodrigo de la Calle's El Invernadero is Madrid's defining green-cuisine fine-dining restaurant. The restaurant's vegetable-led tasting menus, polished technique and sustainability credentials make it essential for diners interested in a lighter, more intellectual version of Spanish gastronomy.
highlights: One-star and green-star vegetable-led restaurant on Ponzano, with a highly personal botanical approach.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Toki is a tiny Japanese haute-cuisine counter from the Marcos Granda orbit, built for diners who value precision, intimacy and rarity. With only a few seats and a focused omakase-style experience, it is one of Madrid's most exclusive small-format Michelin tables.
highlights: One-star six-seat Japanese haute-cuisine counter in Salesas, designed around intimacy and precision.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Javi Estévez has transformed Madrid's traditional offal culture into a Michelin-starred contemporary restaurant. The new Chamberí address gives more comfort and space while preserving the restaurant's visceral, proudly local identity.
highlights: One-star modern offal restaurant, turning traditional casquería into an elegant but characterful Madrid tasting-menu experience.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Eater; Official restaurant website

description: Corral de la Morería's gastronomic restaurant turns one of Madrid's most famous flamenco addresses into a serious fine-dining proposition. The culinary space is small, the wine list is unusually deep, and the setting gives international diners a uniquely Madrid combination of gastronomy, culture and atmosphere.
highlights: One-star restaurant attached to Madrid's landmark flamenco tablao, with a compact dining room and exceptional wine depth.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Eater; Official restaurant website

description: Yugo The Bunker delivers Japanese fine dining with one of Madrid's most distinctive theatrical interiors. Guests move between an izakaya-inspired upper floor and a bunker-like lower space, while the menus focus on serious Japanese product, sake and immersive atmosphere.
highlights: One-star Japanese restaurant in Barrio de las Letras, known for its World War II bunker-inspired lower dining room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Pabú is a small, polished restaurant where Coco Montes channels French influence, microseasonal produce and a very personal Madrid sensibility. The experience feels intimate and contemporary, with enough structure and service polish for an affluent special-occasion dinner.
highlights: One-star microseasonal restaurant in the Castellana area, combining French influence, Spanish product and a compact modern room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: VelascoAbellà brings the pedigree of Óscar Velasco and Montse Abellà into a relaxed but highly capable Chamartín restaurant. The cooking is market-led, precise and deliberately free of unnecessary showmanship, appealing to diners who value confidence, taste and maturity.
highlights: One-star market-cuisine restaurant in Chamartín, with a mature chef-driven style and understated room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Èter is one of Madrid's new Michelin additions, a small Arganzuela restaurant with a contemporary haute-cuisine approach and a personal sibling-run story. It brings energy to a less predictable dining district while keeping the focus on technique, seasonality and emotional clarity.
highlights: New one-star contemporary restaurant in Arganzuela, known for a small scale, personal service and seasonal tasting menus.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Rubén Hernández Mosquero's EMi is a highly anticipated new Madrid fine-dining counter shaped by Nordic ideas, Asian technique and the chef's international résumé. The 12-seat open-kitchen format, ambitious cellar and immediate Michelin recognition make it one of the city's most important recent openings.
highlights: New one-star counter restaurant in Gaztambide, blending New Nordic thinking, Japanese and Korean technique and a serious wine program.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Gofio gives the cuisine of the Canary Islands a sophisticated Madrid stage. Safe Cruz's intimate restaurant is rooted in island memory and produce, but the format, pacing and technique place it firmly in the capital's fine-dining set.
highlights: One-star Canarian tasting-menu restaurant near Gran Vía, with only a small number of diners per service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Chispa Bistró is a compact, design-conscious restaurant near Chueca that turns travel, Mediterranean roots and Japanese influence into a lively Michelin-starred experience. It suits diners looking for serious cooking with a less formal, more cosmopolitan rhythm.
highlights: One-star bistro-style restaurant near Chueca, with Mediterranean cooking, Japanese touches and international inspiration.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Sen Omakase offers one of Madrid's most immersive Japanese tasting menus, built around sushi, kaiseki references and seasonal product. The multi-room experience, high menu price and serious beverage program make it a natural fit for affluent diners seeking Japanese luxury in the capital.
highlights: One-star omakase and kaiseki-inspired experience with 30 to 35 bites and a deep wine list.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Clos Madrid is a polished wine-led restaurant from sommelier Marcos Granda, pairing premium ingredients with a serious cellar in Chamberí. It has a small, luminous room and a service culture that makes it especially appealing to diners who want fine dining without unnecessary spectacle.
highlights: One-star wine-led restaurant in Chamberí, with a glazed wine cellar, small dining room and premium seasonal cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Javier Aranda's Gaytán is built around an open oval kitchen that puts the cooking directly in the dining room. The result is a polished, intimate Michelin experience in Chamartín, with seasonal menus, careful plating and a setting suited to celebrations and high-end business dinners.
highlights: One-star open-kitchen restaurant in Chamartín, with a futuristic dining room and refined tasting-menu format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Sacha is the kind of Madrid restaurant chefs, critics and regulars talk about with unusual affection. It is relaxed rather than formal, but the cooking, product and personality make it essential for an affluent diner who wants a more local, conversational evening.
highlights: Chef-loved Chamartín bistro founded in 1972, famous for warm service, Madrid regulars and a highly personal kitchen.
sources: Madrid Tourism; Eater; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website

description: Lhardy is one of Madrid's great historic dining rooms and a living link to the city's 19th-century luxury restaurant culture. The experience is traditional, formal in feel and deeply atmospheric, with cocido, consommé and old-world service that make it more than a nostalgia stop.
highlights: Historic Madrid institution founded in 1839, known for classic dining rooms, consommé and old-world city elegance.
sources: Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website; Opinionated About Dining

description: Botín is a global landmark as much as a restaurant, but it still functions as a proper Madrid dinner house when approached for roast suckling pig, lamb and historic atmosphere. Its cellars, tiled rooms and long continuity give affluent travelers a culturally meaningful evening that is distinct from the Michelin circuit.
highlights: Founded in 1725 and recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest restaurant, with classic roasts and a historic Austrias setting.
sources: Official restaurant website; Guinness World Records; Madrid Tourism

description: La Bola is a classic Madrid tavern for cocido madrileño, served with the kind of tradition and warmth that makes the dish feel ceremonial rather than merely rustic. It is more relaxed than the fine-dining core, but its history, location and signature preparation make it highly relevant for a sophisticated visitor seeking local identity.
highlights: Century-old Austrias tavern founded in 1870, known for cocido cooked slowly in individual earthenware pots.
sources: Madrid Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: El Cisne Azul is a beloved Chueca mushroom specialist with the feel of a proper Madrid regulars' address. The setting is simple, but the seasonal wild mushrooms, meats and wines give it the kind of focused local character that affluent diners often remember more vividly than another formal tasting menu.
highlights: Long-running Chueca mushroom house, centered on wild mushrooms, Spanish product and a relaxed local evening atmosphere.
sources: Official restaurant website; Condé Nast Traveler; local Madrid dining guides
